Water first. Substrate second. 💧🌱 This is personally my favorite way to add substrate, especially for a no CO₂, no-filter aquarium. I start with about 2 cm of water, then add the substrate directly into it. The water immediately traps most of the fine particles, instead of letting a cloud of dust spread everywhere. I also don’t rinse my substrate, because I prefer to keep everything it contains rather than washing part of the fine material away. Less dust. Less mess. Nothing wasted. Just water first. 🌿 Would you try it this way? New project in collaboration with @aquasistema_es 💚 #aquarium #aquascape #aquascaping #fishtank #plantedtank

Cleaning a fish tank doesn't always mean draining it. In this method, waste and debris are removed while the water stays in place. Tools like siphon vacuums and filtration systems pull out uneaten food, algae, and sediment from the gravel, keeping the environment clean without stressing the fish. What makes this approach effective is balance. Beneficial bacteria remain undisturbed, water chemistry stays stable, and the tank continues to cycle naturally. It's a low-impact way to maintain a healthy aquarium, showing how smart maintenance can work with the ecosystem instead of resetting it. This video is for educational purposes only.
